sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A Linguistic Bibliography of the New Guinea Area. (Pacific Linguistics, D-90.) Canberra: Research School of Pacific and Asian Studies, ANU. [Language index: 'Urimo (SE of Wewak, Sepik) Laycock 1973, Voegelins 1965, W&H 1981'; 'Yaugiba (E Sepik) Voegelins 1965'.]
sources.note: Bibliography, no language data. Its value is negative evidence: as of 1996 the exhaustive New Guinea bibliography knew no work on Urimo beyond Laycock's 1973 checklist, the Voegelins' 1965 listing and the Wurm & Hattori 1981 atlas (Sanders & Sanders 1980 is indexed under the Marienberg/Kamasau entries).

sources.citation: Sanders, Arden G. & Joy Sanders. 1980. Defining the centres of the Marienberg language family. In M. Boxwell, J. Goddard, M. Ross, A. Sanders, J. Sanders & H. Davies (eds), Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 20 (Pacific Linguistics A-56), 171-196. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-A56.171
sources.note: Nothing. A lexicostatistical/sociolinguistic survey of the six Marienberg languages from a 1977 SIL survey; p. 173 states the wordlist data 'was not phonemicised'; Appendix C (p. 195) gives Urimo actor pronouns and verb prefixes only. No phonology, no mention of stress or accent anywhere in pp. 171-196 (a full-text search for stress/accent full text).

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1975. The Torricelli Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 767-780. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Phylum-level phonology paragraph (p. 769): 'three positions of articulation; usually no voicing contrast in consonant phonemes; five to eight vowels.; fairly high proportion of fricative consonants', illustrated from Olo. Urimo occurs only in the population table (Marienberg stock-level family, Urimo 835).

sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Kamasau (kms) is the closest well-described Marienberg relative and the family's linguistic centre per Sanders & Sanders 1980 (Urimo shares 50% cognates with it); a Kamasau stress statement would be the nearest comparative proxy, but it is NOT a statement about Urimo and must not be catalogued as such.
